topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Lena bounced up from the couch, her ponytail springing back into place as she stretched. Her roommate, Mike, was grumbling about the idea of getting a pet, scowling at the cat calendar on their fridge.

"Come on, Mike!" Lena exclaimed, plopping back down beside him with a silly grin. "We can name it Whiskers and have so much fun together! It'll be like having our own little furry friend..."

Mike raised an eyebrow. "_I don't know..._ responsibilities... mess...." He trailed off, but Lena barely noticed, too caught up in her enthusiasm to notice the concern etched on Mike's face.

As they continued arguing, Lena's chatter grew louder and more animated. She flopped her hands around like a conductor leading an orchestra, as if trying to conduct Mike into joining the pet-owning party.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Jen floated through the apartment, twirling back and forth in front of their cluttered living room as she munched on a carrot stick. Her roommate, Emily, sat on the couch, hands clasped behind her head in a defensive pose.

"I _really_ think we should get that cute golden retriever I saw online," Jen chimed in over the phone with her mom (her side of the conversation carried into the kitchen).

Emily frowned at Jen's oblivious exuberance. "I don't know, Jen... it might be too much for us to handle, besides the extra space issue..."

Undeterred, Jen kept prattling on as she continued her energetic dance across the room, an almost musical quality carrying through each step.

When their mom hung up, Emily let out a heavy sigh – but even that was slightly tempered by a glance at Jen's exuberance.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Kaito's eyes sparkled with mischief as he leaned in close to his roommate, Rohan. "Dude, imagine it: we'll wake up every morning to our own tiny pup romping around the living room! Unwind from work, take a walk together..."

Rohan pushed the plate of pad thai farther away, his expression unreadable except for a faint tension creeping into his shoulders.

"I'm not sure that's such a great idea," he cautioned. "Don't get me wrong, but I worry about what with school exams coming up and all these essays – it'd be too much stress on both us..."

Unrelenting, Kaito grinned and clutched Rohan's arm in excitement. As they spoke, the room transformed into a whimsical cartoon, with furry friends flying about their walls like fantastical spirits.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
The apartment fell silent except for Maria pacing back and forth between the living room and kitchen area. Her roommate, Sophia, glared at the calendar plastered across the fridge's middle.

"Sophia, let me convince you..." Maria implored, pausing beside her to gesture dramatically towards the cat calendar.

" _Stop_ pestering me about it," Sophia retorted with a flick of her wrist, but Maria's grin persisted even as Sophia rolled her eyes.

The sounds around them grew muted until only footsteps echoed through the space. Sophia's gaze drifted upward – she was watching Maria instead of her roomie's frantic expression for once.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
In the evening dimness casting across their TV-lit living room, Naomi perched on one leg while reaching out to grab a fallen book, completely at home amidst books and mess. Her roommate, Liam, slumped forward under his jacket laid flat across his laps.

"I mean – why can't we have this little guy?" Naomi asked from behind her long curtain of hair that cascaded over her eyes, fingers fidgeting along with her own internal merriment.

Liam scratched an eyebrow, half-heartedly weighing in on an ongoing debate. As they conversed back and forth across a space shared between couches, their shadows blurred into almost-identical silhouettes against walls as Lena seemed entirely carefree about winning over Liam's opinions.

Each story highlights one aspect of the character's portrayal – how these are presented consistently to convey the emotion at the center and leave room for the reader’s own interpretation.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Lena fidgeted in front of the fridge, drumming her fingers against the side. She had been thinking about it for weeks – the perfect companion to complete their little household. A furry friend would brighten up the place and make coming home from work so much more enjoyable.

As she pulled out a jar of leftover jam, her eyes scanned the kitchen table for any scraps that may have accumulated. Maybe it was best to bring this discussion up over dinner? Jack walked in, yawning, and plopped down beside her on the couch. The TV flickered with an old rerun, but no one seemed interested.

"Hey, we need to talk," Lena said, trying to sound casual while avoiding eye contact. Jack looked up from his phone, confusion evident on his face. "What's up?"

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Mike slumped against the wall by his bed, phone clutched in a white-knuckled grip. The screen glowed bright blue in the dark room – not that it mattered what he was reading these days. He couldn't focus.

His roommate, Alex, burst into the room, still whistling a happy tune from their morning jog. Mike's heart sank at the sound of her energetic voice echoing off the walls. "Morning! Did I miss breakfast?"

Mike forced himself to sit up straighter, though his mind was already elsewhere. The thought of bringing it up then sent a queasy flutter through his stomach. "Nope, still waiting for food to be sorted. By you."

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Samantha scribbled on the walls – her roommates wouldn’t care about some artistic doodles, right? In the corner of the paper where her art lessons lay abandoned, she'd scrawled an almost-invisible message: 'Get a cat.' It was supposed to be her gift for Jack's 24th birthday. Why did mentioning it in person always feel like a betrayal?

Samantha took a deep breath as she stepped into the kitchen. Jack leaned against the counter, pouring himself a glass of water. "Hey, do you smell that? A bit burnt?"

"No," Samantha said calmly. She reached for the coffee maker but her eyes strayed to the cat calendar on the fridge – its cute felines just taunting her at the moment.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Olivia tapped her shoe against the floor as the conversation started in earnest. Maybe it was time for them to put their money where their mouths were? At least, that's what some part of her kept repeating. A pet wasn't just a 'nice idea' – it needed practical planning and a willingness to make sacrifices.

Olivia's voice strained with every step she took towards making this a point of order in their debates: they really did need something fluffy to complete them as roommates. Her eyes scanned the messy living area and her roommate, Jake, who was sprawled across the couch.

"You guys have some pretty valid points about it not being the most practical idea," Olivia admitted quietly, though the corner of her mouth curled up ever so slightly – betraying a hidden excitement.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Ben settled onto his favorite chair by the window and fussed with his worn bookcover. No matter how he dressed it up as a purely theoretical discussion about animal rights, there were still some practical questions he needed to clear up before they really got serious. Too much depended on his roommate's perspective – which could vary wildly from room to night.

"Rachel?" When she finally looked up from her sketchbook, he noticed a faint spark in her eyes that seemed at odds with the way her words were flowing off blandly as usual. Time was running out for him to make some real decisions.

"You're really sold on the idea of getting a pet, aren't you?" The question tumbled out more abruptly than intended – though not in a bad way.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Emma settled into her favorite armchair, phone in hand, scrolling through adoption websites. Her roommate, Rachel, walked into the room, caught up in thought. "I don't think this is a good idea, Emma," she said, her voice firm but hesitant.

Emma looked up, eyes shining with enthusiasm. "What's not to love? We've been talking about getting a pet for months." Rachel sighed and perched on the arm of the chair, looking unsure. Emma nudged her playfully. "Come on, just think about it!"

As they talked, Emma's fingers drummed an impatient rhythm on her knee. Rachel's shoulders seemed to droop under the weight of Emma's excitement.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Max leaned against the kitchen counter, watching as his roommate, Jamie, poured a bowl of kibble for a stray cat that had wandered into their apartment. Max shook his head. "You know we can't just keep it."

Jamie looked up, a gentle smile on his face. His eyes crinkled at the corners as he stroked the cat's soft fur. Max felt a twinge in his chest; maybe this wasn't just about getting a pet – it was about taking care of one.

As they argued, Jamie's gaze darted back and forth between Max and the cat, his hand still gently cupping its head. The tension hung in the air like an unspoken promise.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Lena scribbled furiously on her phone notepad as she brainstormed names for their future pet. Her roommate, Chris, strolled into the room, yawning. "What's all the fuss about?"

Lena looked up, eyes sparkling with excitement, as she read off a list of absurd name combos: Bingo-Schmiko, Sparkles-Monster, and Whiskers-Splat. Chris raised an eyebrow, his voice dripping with amusement. "Those are... um... creative."

Lena felt a flush rise to her cheeks – was Chris just teasing, or did he really get it? As they chatted, she found herself instinctively seeking his approval, her posture easing when he chuckled along.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Kai wandered into the living room, feet bare and toes wiggling. Her roommate, Zara, hunched on the couch, eyes fixed intently on a computer screen displaying adoption statistics. Kai flopped down beside her, making eyes at the cursor as it moved over images of happy furry faces.

Zara turned to her, concern etched on her face. "Kai, we can't afford this." Kai's smile faltered; for a brief moment, she felt like she'd let Zara down. Then something inside her shifted, and her voice took on a determined tone: "We'll figure it out."

Zara watched Kai with an unsure gaze, as if sensing the unspoken tension between them.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Sophia tapped her foot impatiently while watching her roommate, Marcus, make slow progress toward deciding whether to adopt. It was been over an hour since they'd started – they needed food shopping done soon, for goodness' sake! Sophia's gaze darted back and forth across the coffee table where adoption forms lay scattered.

Marcus rubbed his temples, fingers kneading at a tension headache. "Okay, maybe it'll work out," he muttered, eyes squinting as if considering some crucial weight held aloft.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
As Emily paced back and forth across their small living room, her roommate, Sarah, sat on the couch, watching her with an expression of calm patience. The debate had been raging for days: should they get a pet or not? Emily couldn't sleep at night thinking about it, her mind racing with all the worst-case scenarios - fur everywhere, noise complaints from neighbors, vet bills piling up.

Sarah tried to reason with her, explaining that having a pet would bring them closer together, make their apartment feel more like a home. But Emily's worries only seemed to grow. She started to fidget uncontrollably, biting her lip as she muttered under her breath. "We can't afford it," she snapped suddenly, before forcing herself to take a deep breath and calm down.

Sarah leaned in, putting a gentle hand on Emily's arm. "Honey, I understand your concerns, but we can make this work. We'll split the responsibilities, find ways to save money." Emily jerked her arm away, eyes flashing. But as soon as their gazes met, she looked down, and her shoulders slumped.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Jessica slumped against the refrigerator in her dimly lit kitchen, staring blankly at the counter where a makeshift debate zone was set up between herself and her roommate. They'd been talking about getting a pet for what felt like an eternity, but she couldn't bring herself to agree on it. Every thought of moving forward terrified her worse than the last.

As they took turns weighing pros and cons, Jessica's words grew more halting. She stuttered over her sentences, fumbling with phrases like a kid taking a math test under high-pressure. Her voice crackled as she spoke, making her sound even younger and more vulnerable than usual. Her eyes darted around the kitchen as if searching for escape routes.

Her roommate, Alex, patted her hand in an attempt to reassure her that they didn't have to do this alone, that it might be a good chance to bond over shared responsibility. But Jessica yanked her hand away and turned off lights on her side of the counter, effectively severing their discussion.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
The TV played softly in the background as Lucas hunched over his phone on the couch, surrounded by cluttered notes on pet ownership costs and animal welfare services. His roommate Emily pined for a cat to brighten up their small high-rise apartment, but something about it unsettled him deeply.

Each proposal Emily made dug deeper beneath his resolve, her relentless arguing shaking off any lingering tranquility he had after long days of work. He started taking increasingly shorter breaths as if oxygen itself was now scarce and precious - maybe because with a pet would come another bill that'd require more hours spent laboring over paperwork?

Emily paused, confusion etched into the lines around her eyes as she watched him struggle; then stepped back to give some air space after he shook off his sweat-beaded brow. She still wouldn't drop it.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
First-floor apartment living and the anxiety that always accompanied it spilled out of Jasmine through rapid eye movement as she paced, her partner's gentle voice hushed but firm on one side of their argument on whether to welcome a pet. A new creature meant new hazards to monitor every minute of every day – every single thing had potential for chaos when safety was something you constantly worried over.

Their voices started picking up tempo now; it seemed each sentence turned into battle lines drawn out, a whole world being built, one contentious debate at a time. Jasmine's voice caught as her lips pursed in protest against new obligations she didn't feel ready to grapple with; at times, every little tick of uncertainty made the whole concept of a pet seem less appealing.

When confronted with an invitation from her partner to just consider it for two more days, she found herself squirming on her feet like some prey trying desperately to flee a stormy shelter. Her shoulders shrugged off hope when faced with that single looming question still in limbo: whether their lives would truly become simpler after the new responsibility dawned.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Drew trudged behind Matt, who was leading them through cramped hallways towards an out-of-the-way pet store his roommate had convinced him to visit. It didn’t take long for Drew's grip on the coffee mug he'd always carried with him to tighten; now it seemed more necessary than when they were just discussing which place ordered pizzas faster around here.

Inside, their conversation about buying a cat started like any other until Drew lost hold of his nerves completely and dropped the mug as soon as Matt began talking specifics – names to give it, what litter to use, vaccinations. Drew took it upon himself to wander off in pursuit of brochures explaining pet costs from a new financial perspective he'd been trying to sidestep earlier.

Drew's hand started tugging nervously at a crumpled tissue left behind from some other lost or discarded purchase; Matt approached him patiently after what felt like an eternity.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Lena paced back and forth in the living room, her eyes fixed on her roommate Rachel as if daring her to change her mind. The walls seemed to close in around them with every step Lena took. She had been preparing for this argument all day, mentally rehearsing the points she would make, but nothing could have prepared her for Rachel's conviction.

"What's not to love about animals?" Rachel exclaimed, holding up a poster of a fluffy cat. "They're low maintenance, bring us joy...come on!"

But Lena wouldn't be swayed. She halted in front of the TV, her hand on the remote control as if ready to mute Rachel's persuasive words at any moment.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
From where he sat, sprawled across the couch with a stack of books beside him, Ryan watched his roommate Lily pace across the room, her face a picture of dismay. He couldn't help but study every flicker of her expression, searching for that telltale curve to her lip or flutter in her eyes.

Lily stopped abruptly in front of him, her shoulders squaring as if daring him to disagree further. "Ryan, I thought we could finally settle on something around here. But no...we're bickering over pets again."

Her words hung in the air like a challenge. Ryan held still for an uneasy moment before unfolding his legs and sitting up straight.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Emily's hands fluttered around her face as she paced in front of their living room window, where sunlight illuminated her agitation. "I don't understand why you can't see this, Sarah. We're adults. We're perfectly capable of caring for...for that thing."

At 'thing', Sarah opened her mouth to interrupt, but Emily cut her off with a sudden outburst: "It's not just about me! This is something we need to decide together!"

Sarah raised an eyebrow as she watched Emily, sensing some underlying unease in the younger woman.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Mark craned his neck back towards the ceiling, where a faded water stain hung above him like a shadow of doom. "Listen, I get it: you love dogs. But that's no reason to let our entire plan go up in flames."

Below him stood Tom, arms crossed over his chest as if ready to block Mark's objections before they began. Their living room had grown quiet, heavy with the weight of unresolved disagreements.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
She stopped dead in her tracks as it hit her - the momentary confusion giving way to pure, unadulterated frustration. "You can't be serious," Sofia spat at her roommate Chris across the crowded living room.

Chris merely shrugged from his position on the floor cushions. "I think they're cute! We should totally get one."

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Lena stared blankly at the kitchen wall, her eyes unfocused as she wandered around the conversation with Rachel for what felt like the hundredth time. They were discussing getting a pet, and Lena's resistance was starting to wear thin. Rachel had always been the animal lover of the group, but lately, it seemed like all they did was fight about it.

"I don't understand why you're opposed," Rachel said, her voice rising in frustration. "We'd take amazing care of an animal, I promise!" Lena's mind went numb as she tried to process a response. Why couldn't Rachel just see that this wasn't something she wanted?

Lena shrugged, not meeting Rachel's gaze, and wandered over to the coffee maker, searching for something to do with her hands.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Maria walked into the living room, dropping onto the couch in exhaustion. "I don't even know why we're still talking about this," she said, tossing her head back against the cushions. Tom had been bugging her nonstop about getting a pet since they moved in together – first it was cats, then dogs, and now he was obsessed with adopting a giant rabbit.

"I just think it would be great to have something to take care of," Tom said, trying to sound reasonable. Maria felt a wave wash over her, like she'd been hit by a cold draft. She didn't want to hurt his feelings or make him feel guilty for being excited about the idea... but honestly? The thought of more work and responsibility was just overwhelming.

Maria let her head fall forward, scrubbing her eyes with her palms.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
[First-person narration]

I trudged into the kitchen, feeling like I'd been kicked in the stomach. Emily and Mira were in a heated debate about getting a pet – again. I hadn't said a word against it yet, but today's discussion was making me feel suffocated.

Mira: "But we always talked about having a family one day!"

Emily: "I know, I just – Ugh."

The fridge buzzed behind me as I opened the door and mechanically began grabbing stuff for lunch. Emily turned to me, her eyes pleading. For what, I wasn't entirely sure. Maybe a moment of clarity? "Don't you think it would be great?" she said, still trying to wear down my resistance.

I shook my head silently and grabbed a jar of yogurt from the shelf, unable to face the conversation anymore.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Third-person narration

Kael sat on the couch, staring blankly at Rachel as they talked over. They'd been arguing for what felt like hours about adopting a pet – Kael against it – and he was starting to feel... stuck. This situation was becoming more stressful than anything else in his life.

Rachel's words came at him from a distance: "But think of all the fun we'll have with an animal! Cuddling, playing... walking."

Kael blinked once, twice, as thoughts swirled through his mind like dust devils in a storm. He didn't belong here – this was Rachel's territory, not his – and he'd been trying to compromise for weeks now.

He stared at her face, wondering if she truly understood why he couldn't bring himself to say yes.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
[No narration mark]

Lucia slumped against the couch cushions as Emma talked a mile a minute about how awesome having a cat would be. Lucia's fingers drummed on the armrest, a tired beat that had nothing to do with excitement or even consideration. Today wasn't like other days – there just didn't seem to be a way out of this debate.

"...and they're low maintenance!" Emma said brightly, unaware of the storm brewing in Lucia's chest. "No high-pitched howls at 6 am!"

Lucia shook her head faintly, rubbing the dull ache growing between her brows like that might somehow scrub it away.

Emma launched into another point – a string of reasons why getting a cat would be perfect for their little space – but the words blended together on Lucia's eardrums until nothing made sense anymore. She just wished she could escape this endless cycle...

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Emily's eyes widened as she gazed at her roommate, Rachel. "You can't seriously think we need a pet, right?" Emily asked, her voice laced with incredulity.

Rachel shrugged, oblivious to the rising tide of animosity emanating from Emily. "I don't see why not. My niece had a goldfish and it was so cute."

Emily's grip on the couch cushion tightened, her knuckles white. "Cute? You call getting covered in dander or stepping on poop cute?"

Rachel chuckled good-naturedly, completely missing Emily's undertone of revulsion. "Oh, come on, Em! It won't be that bad!"

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Lena stood in the middle of the living room, arms crossed over her chest as she glared at her roommate, Max. "I don't want to talk about this right now," she muttered.

Max was undeterred, sitting down next to Lena on the couch with a grin. "But think about how much fun it'll be! We can name it after our favorite TV show characters!"

Lena's face scrunched in distaste, her eyes darting around the room as if searching for an escape route. She was practically radiating discomfort, but Max just didn't get it.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
First-person narration:

Ugh, my roommate is going to drive me crazy with this pet idea. We've been living together for three years and thought everything was fine, but now she's decided we need some furry menace running around eating our shoes.

I watch as she starts rummaging through the couch cushions, no doubt collecting more junk to contribute to the mess that is already covering every inch of our floor. I shake my head in disgust... or so I tell myself it's not that.

"Seriously, can you just focus on your schoolwork for one minute?" I demand, trying to keep my tone from rising.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Third-person narration:

Alex scowled as he listened to his roommate, Jamie, enthusiastically expounding upon the virtues of their potential new pet. The thought sent a shudder through him – something with fur and claws and shedding hair was not exactly what Alex had signed up for when renting this apartment.

He fidgeted in his seat, drumming out a staccato beat on the armrest as Jamie continued to prattle on about animal welfare and cute puppy pictures. Meanwhile, Alex's stomach rolled over at the prospect of sharing a toilet with some furry beast.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
I trudged into the living room, only half-listening to my roommate's latest lecture about responsible pet ownership. The truth was, I didn't want any part in it – in any form. Even thinking about all those smells and stains makes me queasy.

My friend Rachel walks by just then, eyeing us from across the room with concern. "Hey guys, can I interrupt for a sec? Emily needs to come pick up her packages."

Her words hit me like a slap in the face – a break is exactly what I need right about now.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
As she paced back and forth in front of the living room window, Emily's eyes blazed with a fierce intensity. Her roommate, Rachel, stood still, hands on hips, trying to reason with her again.

"Em, we can get a cat, I promise," Rachel said, attempting to placate her friend. "It'll be low-maintenance, and we can take turns feeding it."

Emily's jaw clenched as she turned away from the window. Her fists were curled at her sides, knuckles white with tension.

"You don't understand," Emily snapped, spinning back around. "We can barely afford our rent, let alone some pet's food and vet bills!"

Rachel sighed, rubbing her temples. "Fine. We'll look for free options or cheap alternatives. But we need something to liven up this apartment."

Emily's shoulders tensed, her eyes sparking with a fire that made Rachel take a step back.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Lena flopped down on the couch, folding her arms across her chest as she stared at her roommate across from her. Mike had finally brought out the white-paws posters and pamphlets for what felt like an hour.

"Just look how cute it would be!" Mike exclaimed, holding up a poster of two kittens snuggling together.

Lena scoffed, rolling her eyes so hard they nearly got stuck that way. "It's going to cost us both more in vet bills than we're saving on the couch situation right now."

Mike's face reddened as he realized Lena was about to shut him down for good this time.

"Come on, Lena! It'll be fun, and great practice for you before we go get a real kid later."

Lena's lips pursed, her face setting in an unyielding expression that kept Mike quiet.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
First-person narrative:

As I sat at the kitchen table with my roommate Mark across from me, I felt this crawling sensation under my skin that just wouldn't quit. He had this goofy grin plastered on his face as he rambled on about how much we'd love having a cat in our apartment.

Look, it's not the money per se – though we do have better things to spend our hard-earned cash on than pet food or emergency vet trips. No, it's more about principle for me. I value our freedom as roommates and friends far too much to just indulge him here.

I pressed my lips together firmly as Mark launched into his counterpoints: how we needed something to liven up the apartment, how we could even get the neighbors on board, and so forth.

"Mark?" I interrupted coolly, raising an eyebrow for a dramatic effect. "How about if we, uh, actually did some stuff around here besides just daydreaming?"

My eyes narrowed slightly as Mark's grin faltered.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Mia yanked open the refrigerator door, making a beeline straight for the leftovers stashed on the top shelf. Her roommate Jamie was perched on the windowsill, arms wrapped around her knees and gazing off into space.

"...And just think how awesome it'll be when we get our new couch – the cat will have its own cushion!"

Mia snatched up a Tupperware container she wasn't exactly sure what leftovers were anymore. It was some science-y meal from college that had long since gone inedible, even for Jamie's taste.

"Oh, joy," I muttered under my breath as I yanked the fridge door shut behind me and stomped out of the kitchen ahead. "I'll believe it when our bank account doesn't look like a disaster waiting to happen."

Mia stopped mid-stride down the hallway and pivoted sharply on one foot. Her eyes locked onto Jamie's oblivious form.

"Jamie?" I called, my voice loud enough for her roommate's ears – but with an edge that made even Jamie twitch.

topic: Two roommates disagree about getting a pet
story:
Alex slammed his laptop shut so hard it bounced off the living room coffee table as he stood up from his chair, eyes wide with incredulity. His roommate Lucas was grinning at him like a simpleton in one of those 'We Have Pet Cuddling Now!' videos.

"I don't pay for rent to raise some other creature's offspring," Alex retorted darkly. "And besides – it wasn't exactly the agreed-upon conversation topic during that White Elephant game last weekend!"

The tension between them coagulated so starkly in this small, cluttered space that even I thought about stepping aside and hiding until my roommates worked things out.

But nope – Lucas kept on soldiering forward. And as he kept going, I found myself taking a small step backward into the kitchen shadows.
